title: Sir Philip Sidney
author: James Baldwin
summary: 菲利普·西德尼爵士在战场上把救命的水让给更需要的垂死士兵。
publicDomainBasis: Published 1896 by the American Book Company; author James Baldwin (1841–1925). Public domain in the United States and in China (author's life plus 70 years).

paragraphs.en: A cruel battle was being fought. The ground was covered with dead and dying men. The air was hot and stifling. The sun shone down without pity on the wounded soldiers lying in the blood and dust.
paragraphs.zh: 一场残酷的战斗正在进行。地上躺满了死者和垂死的人。空气闷热得令人窒息。太阳无情地照在躺在血泊和尘土中的伤兵身上。

paragraphs.en: One of these soldiers was a nobleman, whom everybody loved for his gentleness and kindness. Yet now he was no better off than the poorest man in the field. He had been wounded, and would die; and he was suffering much with pain and thirst.
paragraphs.zh: 其中一名士兵是一位贵族，他性情温和、心地善良，人人都爱戴他。可此刻，他的处境并不比战场上最贫穷的人好。他受了伤，快要死了，正承受着剧烈的疼痛和干渴。

paragraphs.en: When the battle was over, his friends hurried to his aid. A soldier came running with a cup in his hand.
paragraphs.zh: 战斗结束后，朋友们赶忙来救他。一名士兵手里端着杯子跑了过来。

paragraphs.en: "Here, Sir Philip," he said, "I have brought you some clear, cool water from the brook. I will raise your head so that you can drink."
paragraphs.zh: “来，菲利普爵士，”他说，“我从溪里给您取了些清凉的水。我扶您抬起头，您喝一点吧。”

paragraphs.en: The cup was placed to Sir Philip's lips. How thankfully he looked at the man who had brought it! Then his eyes met those of a dying soldier who was lying on the ground close by. The wistful look in the poor man's face spoke plainer than words.
paragraphs.zh: 杯子送到了菲利普爵士唇边。他满怀感激地望着端水来的士兵！这时，他的目光遇上了躺在近旁地上的一名垂死士兵的眼睛。那可怜人脸上渴望的神情，比言语更清楚。

paragraphs.en: "Give the water to that man," said Sir Philip quickly; and then, pushing the cup toward him, he said, "Here, my comrade, take this. Thy need is greater than mine."
paragraphs.zh: “把水给那个人。”菲利普爵士立刻说；他把杯子推向那人，“来，我的同伴，把这个喝了吧。你比我更需要它。”

paragraphs.en: What a brave, noble man he was! The name of Sir Philip Sidney will never be forgotten; for it was the name of a Christian gentleman who always had the good of others in his mind. Was it any wonder that everybody wept when it was heard that he was dead?
paragraphs.zh: 他是多么勇敢、高尚的人啊！菲利普·西德尼爵士的名字永远不会被遗忘，因为这是一个基督徒绅士的名字，他心里总是装着别人的福祉。当人们听说他去世时，人人落泪，这又有什么奇怪呢？

paragraphs.en: It is said, that, on the day when he was carried to the grave, every eye in the land was filled with tears. Rich and poor, high and low, all felt that they had lost a friend; all mourned the death of the kindest, gentlest man that they had ever known.
paragraphs.zh: 据说，在他被送往墓地的那天，这片土地上人人眼中含泪。无论贫富、无论高低，大家都觉得自己失去了一位朋友；大家都为这个他们见过的最善良、最温和的人哀悼。
